title: 658. Dawn of the Samurai: The Shadow of the Sword (Part 1)

sentences.en: The Mongol Empire is invading our home.
sentences.zh: 蒙古帝国正在入侵我们的家园。

sentences.en: They are brutal, relentless, unstoppable.
sentences.zh: 他们残暴、无情、势不可挡。

sentences.en: We are 80 samurai against an army, fighting to slow the invasion.
sentences.zh: 我们只有80名武士对抗一支大军，我们要拼死延缓他们的入侵。

sentences.en: Today, I die for my people.
sentences.zh: 今天，我为我的人民而死。

sentences.en: There must be thousands of the enemy.
sentences.zh: 敌人一定有数千之众。

sentences.en: We will face death and defend our home.
sentences.zh: 我们将直面死亡，保卫我们的家园。

sentences.en: Tradition, courage, honor.
sentences.zh: 传统、勇气、荣誉。

sentences.en: They are what make us.
sentences.zh: 这些造就了我们。

sentences.en: We are the warriors of Tsushima.
sentences.zh: 我们是对马岛的战士。

sentences.en: We are samurai.
sentences.zh: 我们是武士。

sentences.en: Konnichiwa, everybody.
sentences.zh: 大家好。

sentences.en: So that is the opening to the excellent video game, Ghost of Tsushima, which was developed by an American company, Sucker Punch Productions for Sony, in 2020.
sentences.zh: 这就是那款优秀电子游戏《对马岛之魂》的开场，该游戏由美国Sucker Punch Productions公司为索尼开发，于2020年发行。

sentences.en: And as anyone who's played the game will know, we're in the 13th century in 1274.
sentences.zh: 正如所有玩过这款游戏的人所知，故事背景设定在13世纪的1274年。

sentences.en: So the antagonists are the Mongols, who are ruling a mighty empire, stretching all the way from the Danube to the peninsula of Korea.
sentences.zh: 反派是蒙古人，他们统治着一个强大的帝国，版图从多瑙河一直延伸到朝鲜半岛。

sentences.en: And their next target is Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们的下一个目标是日本。

sentences.en: And a huge Mongol armada is on the way.
sentences.zh: 一支庞大的蒙古舰队正在赶来。

sentences.en: And the first stop in its sights is Tsushima, which is the island that lies midway between Korea and Western Japan.
sentences.zh: 它瞄准的第一个目标是对马岛，也就是位于朝鲜和日本西部之间的一座岛屿。

sentences.en: And in the game, you are playing as Jin Sakai.
sentences.zh: 在游戏中，你扮演的是境井仁。

sentences.en: So your task is to resist the Mongol assault.
sentences.zh: 你的任务是抵抗蒙古人的进攻。

sentences.en: And you are a young nobleman of Tsushima.
sentences.zh: 你是对马岛的一名年轻贵族。

sentences.en: And you've been instructed in the way of the samurai by your uncle, Lord Shimura, who is the person speaking in that prologue.
sentences.zh: 你的叔叔志村大人——也就是刚才序幕中说话的那个人——教导你武士之道。

sentences.en: And in fact, one of the things you have to do in the game is to slightly ignore Shimura's advice, because you're playing as a ghost, a kind of assassin.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你在游戏中必须做的一件事，就是稍微无视志村大人的建议，因为你扮演的是一名“战鬼”，一种类似于刺客的角色。

sentences.en: Because Shimura says to you at the beginning,
sentences.zh: 因为志村在开头对你说：

sentences.en: Jin, when we fight, we face our enemy head on.
sentences.zh: “仁，当我们战斗时，我们要正面迎敌。”

sentences.en: And when we take their life, we look them in the eye with courage and respect.
sentences.zh: “当我们夺取他们的生命时，我们要带着勇气和尊重直视他们的双眼。”

sentences.en: This is what makes us samurai.
sentences.zh: “这就是武士的准则。”

sentences.en: But whether Jin heeds that advice or whether he goes his own way is what the game is about, isn't it, Tom?
sentences.zh: 但仁是听从了建议，还是走上了自己的道路，这正是游戏的主题，对吧，汤姆？

sentences.en: You're such a big video games fan.
sentences.zh: 你可是个超级电子游戏迷。

sentences.en: I'm amazed you started this with such a long discussion about Ghost of Tsushima.
sentences.zh: 我很惊讶你竟然用这么长的篇幅来讨论《对马岛之魂》。

sentences.en: I mean, it's an excellent choice.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这是一个极好的选择。

sentences.en: But I'm guessing you've never played it?
sentences.zh: 但我猜你从来没玩过它？

sentences.en: I looked at it on YouTube, thought it looked quite good, quite exciting.
sentences.zh: 我在YouTube上看过，觉得看起来很不错，挺刺激的。

sentences.en: And I wanted to do that partly because the samurai are such a part of kind of video game culture.
sentences.zh: 我之所以想这么做，部分原因是因为武士在某种程度上是电子游戏文化的一部分。

sentences.en: Am I right in saying that?
sentences.zh: 我这么说对吗？

sentences.en: I think I am.
sentences.zh: 我想我是对的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: I mean, there's lots of samurai video games.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有很多关于武士的电子游戏。

sentences.en: But it's also because that opening that you gave, it's expressive of a very distinctive take, a very distinctive understanding of the samurai.
sentences.zh: 但这也是因为你刚才给出的那段开场白，表达了一种非常独特的视角，一种对武士非常独特的理解。

sentences.en: The actual reality, the historical context,
sentences.zh: 关于实际的现实，历史背景，

sentences.en: you know, what actually happened when the Mongols landed at Tsushima.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当蒙古人登陆对马岛时到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: They then go on to attack mainland Japan.
sentences.zh: 他们随后继续进攻日本本土。

sentences.en: We will be coming to that later in this year.
sentences.zh: 我们今年晚些时候会讲到这一点。

sentences.en: We're not going to be doing that in this series because in this series, we're going back to look at the beginnings of the samurai, the origins of this extraordinary warrior caste.
sentences.zh: 我们不会在这个系列中讲，因为在这个系列里，我们要回溯武士的起源，探究这个非凡战士阶级的由来。

sentences.en: And it's a story that will be taking us to the heart of medieval Japan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个将带我们深入中世纪日本核心的故事。

sentences.en: So we'll be going to the 10th, the 11th centuries, when this very distinctive class of warrior starts to emerge on the Japanese archipelago.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将回到10世纪和11世纪，那时这种非常独特的战士阶级开始在日本列岛上出现。

sentences.en: We'll be looking particularly at the eruption in the late 12th century of this massive civil war between rival samurai clans.
sentences.zh: 我们将特别关注12世纪末，敌对武士氏族之间爆发的那场大规模内战。

sentences.en: And this is a conflict that inspired the great epic of medieval Japan, the kind of the Iliad of Japan, which is a work called The Tale of the Heike.
sentences.zh: 这场冲突激发了中世纪日本的伟大史诗，也就是日本的《伊利亚特》，一部名为《平家物语》的作品。

sentences.en: And we will also be exploring the way in which the rise of military rule, the rise of this warrior caste results in the eclipse of the traditional court life
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨军事统治的兴起，这个战士阶级的崛起如何导致了传统宫廷生活的衰落，

sentences.en: focused in Kyoto, the great imperial capital.
sentences.zh: 那种以伟大的帝国首都京都为中心的宫廷生活。

sentences.en: So it's a series about a cast of warriors who rank, I would say, as perhaps the most glamorous and mythologized warriors of all time.
sentences.zh: 所以这是一个关于战士阶级的系列，我认为他们或许是有史以来最迷人、最被神话的战士。

sentences.en: Yeah, lots of our listeners will have a vague impression of the samurai, I would imagine.
sentences.zh: 是的，我想我们的许多听众对武士都有一个模糊的印象。

sentences.en: They'll imagine the drawn swords and the tremendous armor and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们会想象出拔出的刀剑、威武的盔甲之类的东西。

sentences.en: But I'm guessing a lot of people have only the very flimsiest idea of exactly when they were around and where they came from.
sentences.zh: 但我猜很多人对于他们究竟存在于何时、来自何处，只有非常模糊的概念。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And I think because they are so mythologized, it's probably worthwhile before we actually start the chronological sweep of this series,
sentences.zh: 我认为因为他们被神话得太厉害了，所以在我们开始这个系列的时间线梳理之前，非常有必要，

sentences.en: go back to the beginnings of how and why the samurai emerge.
sentences.zh: 回溯武士是如何以及为何出现的开端。

sentences.en: I think it's worth giving listeners a sense of the broad sweep of their history so that we can put their emergence in an overall context.
sentences.zh: 我认为有必要让听众对他们的历史有一个宏观的了解，这样我们才能把他们的出现放在一个整体的背景中。

sentences.en: So as you say, if you shut your eyes, if you imagine a samurai, I think the image is likely to be that of a warrior vaguely situated in the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，如果你闭上眼睛，想象一个武士，我认为这个形象很可能是一个模糊地处于中世纪的战士。

sentences.en: So actually someone like Jin Sakai in Ghost of Tsushima.
sentences.zh: 就像《对马岛之魂》里的境井仁那样。

sentences.en: But the thing about the samurai, and this is what makes them different, say, from other very mythologized classes of warrior like Vikings, say,
sentences.zh: 但武士的特别之处在于——这也是他们区别于其他被高度神话的战士阶级的地方，比如维京人，

sentences.en: or the knights of medieval Christendom.
sentences.zh: 或者中世纪基督教世界的骑士。

sentences.en: These are medieval warriors who actually outlast the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 他们是中世纪的战士，却活过了中世纪。

sentences.en: And I think that this is why in the West, as well as I would guess in Japan,
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是为什么在西方，以及我想在日本也是如此，

sentences.en: their aesthetic, the sense of them as having kind of moral codes, their vibe, if you want to put it
sentences.zh: 他们的美学，他们那种拥有道德准则的感觉，或者如果你愿意的话，他们的“氛围”，

sentences.en: like that, can actually seem much more attuned to contemporary culture than, say, those of Harold
sentences.zh: 实际上看起来比哈拉尔德·哈德拉达（伟大的维京战士）或黑太子（中世纪骑士精神的典范）更契合当代文化。

sentences.en: Hardrada, the great Viking warrior, or the Black Prince, the flower of medieval chivalry.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为这反过来又揭示了武士在人们想象中地位的另一个悖论，即一方面，他们是不可磨灭的日本象征。

sentences.en: And I think that this in turn underlies a further paradox about the standing of the samurai in the imagination, which is that on the one hand, they are indelibly Japanese.
sentences.zh: 他们与艺伎、茶道、相扑等一起，作为日本文化的一流标志。

sentences.en: They are up there with geisha and with tea ceremonies and sumo and all that kind of thing as absolutely kind of A-list markers of Japanese culture.
sentences.zh: 武士就是日本。

sentences.en: A samurai is Japan.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他们也成为了全球偶像。

sentences.en: But at the same time, they have also become global icons.
sentences.zh: 他们是普遍着迷的对象。

sentences.en: They are objects of a universal fascination.
sentences.zh: 所以当你进行《对马岛之魂》的开场白时，你的口音是一种美日融合的风格，这在某种程度上正是武士所演变的样子。

sentences.en: So when you did that opening to the Ghost of Tsushima, your accent was a kind of American-Japanese fusion, which is kind of what the samurai has become.
sentences.zh: 是的，而且还有一种微妙的，不完全是永恒的感觉，

sentences.en: Yeah, and there's something also slightly, not exactly timeless,
sentences.zh: 但武士已经脱离了他们的时代，所以你经常能在武士身上看到非常科幻的东西。

sentences.en: but the samurai have been detached from their epoch so that they can often see in something very science fiction about the samurai.
sentences.zh: 例如，武士对《星球大战》的影响就是一个很好的例子，这也是你将要讨论的内容。

sentences.en: So the samurai's influence on Star Wars, for example, is a case in point, which is something you'll be discussing.
sentences.zh: 这一点在大英博物馆目前举办的关于武士的展览中得到了精彩的展示。

sentences.en: This is brilliantly illustrated in a show that's on at the British Museum at the moment about the samurai.
sentences.zh: 你走进这个展览，第一个展品，灯光布置得非常精美，是一套令人毛骨悚然的盔甲。

sentences.en: And you walk into this show and the very first exhibit, beautifully lit, is this incredibly eerie suit of armour.
sentences.zh: 你有一个头盔。

sentences.en: So you have a helmet.
sentences.zh: 它配有一个面具。

sentences.en: It's complete with a kind of face mask.
sentences.zh: 眉间有一个龙首。

sentences.en: It's got a dragon's head over the brows.
sentences.zh: 从头盔后面伸出来的是看起来非常阴森的金叶。

sentences.en: And coming from the back of the helmet, there are these golden leaves that look very sinister.
sentences.zh: 它们看起来就像某种刀刃。

sentences.en: They're like kind of blades.
sentences.zh: 有一件铁胸甲。

sentences.en: There's an iron cuirass.
sentences.zh: 有丝绸系带的腿甲。

sentences.en: There are thigh guards that are laced with silk.
sentences.zh: 有丝绸内衬的袖子和护胫。

sentences.en: There are sleeves and shin guards that are lined with silk.
sentences.zh: 这套装备的各个部分来自16世纪和17世纪。

sentences.en: And the various parts of this outfit come from the 16th and 17th centuries.
sentences.zh: 这就是日本历史上大变革前夕武士的装束。

sentences.en: And so this is the look of the samurai on the cusp of the great transformation in Japan's history.
sentences.zh: 这是对近200年内战的救赎，那场横跨整个15和16世纪的战士氏族间的混战。

sentences.en: And this is its redemption from what had been almost 200 years of internecine civil war fighting between warrior clans that had spanned the whole of the 15th and 16th centuries.
sentences.zh: 它被称为“战国时代”，类似于中国历史上的战国时期。

sentences.en: And it's known as the age of the warring states after a similar period of war in Chinese history.
sentences.zh: 然后在1603年，一位军阀终于成功确立了他对整个日本的统治。

sentences.en: And then in 1603, a single warlord finally manages to establish his supremacy over the whole of Japan.
sentences.zh: 他击败了他所有的敌对军阀。

sentences.en: He defeats all his kind of the rival warlords.
sentences.zh: 这个人叫德川家康。

sentences.en: And this is a man called Tokugawa Yeyasu.
sentences.zh: 对于那些看过《幕府将军》的人来说——那部设定在1600年的精彩迪士尼剧集——他就是吉井虎长大人的原型，

sentences.en: And he, for those who have seen Shogun, the wonderfully good Disney series set in the year 1600, this is the model for Lord Toronaga,
sentences.zh: 他同样会在《幕府将军》中成为幕府将军。

sentences.en: who will likewise in Shogun emerge as the Shogun.
sentences.zh: “幕府将军”这个头衔，是一个古老的头衔，对吧？

sentences.en: And the title Shogun, so Shogun is an ancient title, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 或者至少在它的完整版本中，它是一个古老的头衔。

sentences.en: Or at least in its full version, it's an ancient title.
sentences.zh: 它基本上是指征讨蛮夷的大将军或军阀。

sentences.en: And it's basically a great general or warlord who subdues barbarians.
sentences.zh: 不是这样吗？

sentences.en: Isn't that right?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 所以它实际上有点像“统帅”（Imperator），就是大西庇阿获得的那个词。

sentences.en: So it's actually, it's a little bit like imperator, the word that Scipio Africanus was given.
sentences.zh: 所以它是一位战胜了蛮夷的胜利将军，正如你所说。

sentences.en: So it's a victorious general who's triumphed over kind of barbarians, as you say.
sentences.zh: 在日语中，这个词“幕府将军”有着非常高贵的血统。

sentences.en: In Japanese, this word Shogun has a very classy pedigree.
sentences.zh: 它一直追溯到日本国家的最早期，那是一个……的时期。

sentences.en: It goes right the way back to the earliest days of the Japanese state, which is a period when...
sentences.zh: 所以日本的地理在这个故事中将非常重要。

sentences.en: So the geography of Japan is going to be quite important in this story.
sentences.zh: 如果你想到日本的主岛，中心岛屿本州岛，中间有一大片山脉贯穿其中。

sentences.en: So if you think of the main island of Japan, the central island, Honshu, there's a great kind of block of mountains right running through the middle of it.
sentences.zh: 日本约75%的土地是山地。

sentences.en: And about 75% of Japan is mountainous.
sentences.zh: 在那一侧的西部，一切都是文明的。

sentences.en: And on the western side of that, it's all civilized.
sentences.zh: 这是中世纪早期日本帝国国家的中心，位于这片大山脉的北部。

sentences.en: This is where the Japanese imperial state is centered in the early Middle Ages and north of this great block of mountains.
sentences.zh: 也就是本州岛的东北部。

sentences.en: So in northeastern Honshu.
sentences.zh: 在中世纪早期，这里住满了日本人所说的“蛮夷”。

sentences.en: This in the early Middle Ages is full of what are called by the Japanese barbarians.
sentences.zh: 所以将军们从伟大的帝国宫廷京都被派往北方荒野去征讨这些蛮夷。

sentences.en: And so generals get sent from Kyoto, the great imperial court, to go and fight these barbarians in the kind of the northern wilds.
sentences.zh: 德川家康通过采用“幕府将军”这个头衔，通过利用这些古老的传统，刻意地使其政权合法化。

sentences.en: And Tokugawa Ieyasu, by taking this title of Shogun, is deliberately legitimizing his regime by drawing on these kind of ancient traditions.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常熟悉的故事。

sentences.en: It's a very familiar story.
sentences.zh: 一种激进的、革命性的新政府形式，在传统的掩护下美化并掩盖了它的激进性。

sentences.en: A radical, revolutionary new form of government dignifies and disguises its radicalism beneath a show of tradition.
sentences.zh: 所以实际上，德川现在是政府首脑。

sentences.en: So effectively, Tokugawa is now the head of government.
sentences.zh: 他管理国家。

sentences.en: He runs the state.
sentences.zh: 但在法律上，就像中世纪早期的将军们一样，他的地位是天皇的臣子。

sentences.en: But legally, like the generals back in the early Middle Ages, he is ranking as a servant of the emperor.
sentences.zh: 这就是法律上的情况。

sentences.en: That is the kind of the legal situation.
sentences.zh: 德川建立并由其后代管理的政权持续了两个半世纪。

sentences.en: And the regime that Tokugawa establishes, and which is run by his descendants, endures for two and a half centuries.
sentences.zh: 一直持续到19世纪中叶。

sentences.en: So right the way up until the middle of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 在整个期间，日本保持了和平。

sentences.en: And throughout that entire period, Japan remains at peace.
sentences.zh: 所以你经历了200年的残酷战争，军阀们互相残杀，然后是两个半世纪的稳定与秩序。

sentences.en: So you've had 200 years of kind of savage war, warlords tearing chunks out of each other, and then you have two and a half centuries of stability and order.
sentences.zh: 但疯狂的是，或者说也许并不疯狂。

sentences.en: But the mad thing is, well, maybe it's not mad.
sentences.zh: 我是说，也许这反映了德川达成的和解。

sentences.en: I mean, maybe it's reflective of the settlement that Tokugawa has arrived at.
sentences.zh: 在整个和平时期，武士实际上是作为官僚、作为文职人员在运作。

sentences.en: Throughout this period of peace, the samurai are effectively functioning as bureaucrats, as civilians.
sentences.zh: 但他们从未放弃他们的军事身份。

sentences.en: But they never give up their military status.
sentences.zh: 幕府始终将自己塑造为一个军事政权。

sentences.en: The shogunate is always casting itself as a military regime.
sentences.zh: 所以武士，这些战士，总共不到人口的10%，但他们被列为上层阶级。

sentences.en: So the samurai, the warriors, are less than 10% of the population in all, but they rank as the kind of the upper class.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意这么说的话，他们是最高贵的阶级。

sentences.en: The kind of the most prestigious caste, if you want to put it that way.
sentences.zh: 因为除了出身，几乎不可能成为武士。

sentences.en: Because it's almost impossible to become a samurai except by birth.
sentences.zh: 即使他们基本上把时间花在组织劳役、修路之类的事务上，作为文职人员运作，

sentences.en: And even though they are basically spending their time, you know, organising, I don't know, corvets or roads or whatever, they're functioning as civilians,
sentences.zh: 他们仍有义务保持一种名义上的军事备战状态。

sentences.en: they are obliged to maintain a kind of nominal state of military readiness.
sentences.zh: 而且你的武士地位越高，出身越好，你就越被期望像战国时代的领主那样去“角色扮演”。

sentences.en: And the grander you are as a samurai, the better your birth, the more you are expected to kind of cosplay as a lord from the era of the warring states.
sentences.zh: 所以这其中有一种装扮和角色扮演的成分，不是吗？

sentences.en: So there is an element of dressing up and roleplaying about this, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 一种刻意的、自觉的角色扮演，几乎是这样。

sentences.en: A deliberate, self-conscious roleplaying, almoSt.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就好像在维多利亚时代的上议院，议员们必须穿着盔甲出席一样。

sentences.en: I mean, it's as though in the Victorian House of Lords, the lords had to come dressed in armour.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 保持武士的形象很重要，这样他们才能在万一发生蒙古人再次入侵之类的事情时做好准备。

sentences.en: It's important to the image of the samurai that they are ready in case, you know, a repeat of the Mongol attack happens or something like that.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 所以武士领主们从小就被教导骑马、在马背上射箭。

sentences.en: So samurai lords are brought up to ride a horse, to shoot arrows from horseback.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有剑术，武士刀，那种著名的带有弧形刀刃的日本刀，

sentences.en: Of course, the swordsmanship, the katana, the famous Japanese sword with its curved blade and, you know,
sentences.zh: 你用双手握住刀柄，并将它刀刃向上佩戴在腰间。

sentences.en: you have the hilt that you hold with two hands and you wear it blade up at the waiSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，盔甲起源于战国时代。

sentences.en: You know, the armour originates in the period of the warring state.
sentences.zh: 所以胸甲、护胫、金属面具、头盔，这些头盔上装饰着非常壮观的身份标志，新月、翅膀、动物头颅。

sentences.en: So the breastplates, the shin guards, the metal masks, the helmets, and these helmets are adorned with really spectacular markers of identity, crescent moons, wings, animal heads.
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上就是你在大英博物馆展览开幕时看到的盔甲。

sentences.en: So this is basically the armour that you see at the opening of the British Museum show.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们穿着这些装备扮演着中世纪战士的角色。

sentences.en: And as you say, they are playing the part of medieval warriors with all this stuff.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，当他们穿着壮观的头盔，练习骑术，学习射箭时，在外部世界，

sentences.en: And at the same time, as they are dressing up in their spectacular helmets and practising their horsemanship and learning to fire bow and arrow, in the outside world,
sentences.zh: 尤其是西方世界，生活仍在继续。

sentences.en: and particularly the Western world, life goes on.
sentences.zh: 当然在欧洲，人们对日本几乎一无所知。

sentences.en: And certainly in Europe, people are pretty oblivious to Japan.
sentences.zh: 当然在欧洲，人们对日本几乎一无所知。

sentences.en: And this is because Japan has shut itself off.
sentences.zh: 这是因为日本当时实行了闭关锁国政策。

sentences.en: So there is one isolated factory that is on an island off Nagasaki in the southwest of Japan.
sentences.zh: 当时在长崎外海的一个岛上，有一座与世隔绝的工厂。

sentences.en: And this is run by the Dutch.
sentences.zh: 它由荷兰人经营。

sentences.en: And the Dutch are the only Europeans who are allowed to have a presence on Japanese soil.
sentences.zh: 荷兰人是当时唯一被允许在日本领土上驻留的欧洲人。

sentences.en: So by the 19th century, Europeans have effectively been banned from Japan for over 200 years.
sentences.zh: 所以到了19世纪，欧洲人实际上已经被日本拒之门外超过200年了。

sentences.en: And then in 1853, it all changes.
sentences.zh: 直到1853年，一切都改变了。

sentences.en: Because a US Commodore called Matthew Perry sails into what would come to be called Tokyo Bay at the head of four menacing ships, as it seems to the Japanese.
sentences.zh: 因为一位名叫马修·佩里的美国海军准将，率领着四艘在日本人看来极具威胁的军舰，驶入了后来被称为东京湾的海域。

sentences.en: Four black ships, they're called.
sentences.zh: 也就是所谓的“黑船”。

sentences.en: Yeah, the black ships.
sentences.zh: 没错，就是黑船。

sentences.en: And the Americans, you know, they've got their guns and their cannon and everything.
sentences.zh: 而且美国人带着他们的枪炮和各种装备。

sentences.en: So they are able to force a hearing from the shogunate.
sentences.zh: 所以他们能够强迫幕府听取他们的要求。

sentences.en: And they land in Edo, as it's called, the great city.
sentences.zh: 他们登陆了当时被称为江户的伟大城市。

sentences.en: And they find something that seems to them completely wild, which is this fantastical land where history seems to have been put on hold.
sentences.zh: 他们发现了一些在他们看来完全不可思议的事情，这是一个仿佛历史停滞了的奇幻国度。

sentences.en: You know, it seems like the Middle Ages are still kind of running.
sentences.zh: 你知道，感觉就像中世纪还在延续一样。

sentences.en: I mean, this isn't entirely the case.
sentences.zh: 当然，这并不完全准确。

sentences.en: So it's often said that the shogunate banned firearms, for instance.
sentences.zh: 人们常说幕府禁止了火器，例如。

sentences.en: This isn't true.
sentences.zh: 这并非事实。

sentences.en: What they do is to regulate the use of firearms very, very strictly.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上是对火器的使用进行了非常、非常严格的管制。

sentences.en: So it often seemed to European visitors that there weren't firearMs.
sentences.zh: 所以欧洲访客往往觉得那里没有火器。

sentences.en: There were.
sentences.zh: 其实是有的。

sentences.en: But it's undoubtedly the case that Japan compared, say, to the industrializing states of Europe or the United States in the middle of the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 但毫无疑问，与19世纪中叶欧洲或美国的工业化国家相比，日本的情况确实如此。

sentences.en: I mean, it does seem really, really weird.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这看起来真的非常、非常怪异。

sentences.en: This land ruled by a kind of medieval order of warriors in the age of the steam train and the telegraph and battleships and all of that.
sentences.zh: 在蒸汽火车、电报和战舰的时代，这个国家竟然由一种中世纪的武士秩序统治着。

sentences.en: But now that Commodore Perry has arrived in Tokyo Bay and kind of opened Japan up to the world,
sentences.zh: 但现在佩里准将抵达了东京湾，某种程度上向世界打开了日本的大门，

sentences.en: this is very bad news for the rule of the samurai because they're going to force Japan to open up.
sentences.zh: 这对武士的统治来说是非常糟糕的消息，因为他们将迫使日本开放。

sentences.en: And this is not good news for, you know, ancient medieval warriors.
sentences.zh: 这对那些古老的中世纪武士来说可不是什么好消息。

sentences.en: No, no.
sentences.zh: 确实不是。

sentences.en: There's a nice book on people who are interested, a sort of short history of Japan by Christopher Harding, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 对于感兴趣的人，克里斯托弗·哈丁写过一本不错的书，一本关于日本的简史，对吧？

sentences.en: Who's been on the show during the World Cup.
sentences.zh: 他曾在世界杯期间上过我们的节目。

sentences.en: And he has a story about an Earl of Samurai going to America, which perfectly captures the kind of culture clash, doesn't it?
sentences.zh: 他讲了一个关于武士伯爵去美国的故事，完美地捕捉到了那种文化冲突，不是吗？

sentences.en: Is that 1860?
sentences.zh: 那是1860年吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So it's the first embassy that goes from Japan to a Western country, and it's taken on an American ship across the Pacific.
sentences.zh: 那是日本派往西方国家的第一个使团，他们乘坐美国船只横跨太平洋。

sentences.en: They land in San Francisco, and they find everything about America bewildering.
sentences.zh: 他们抵达旧金山，发现关于美国的一切都令人困惑。

sentences.en: So there's a tremendous account of the samurai having their first American food.
sentences.zh: 有一段关于武士第一次吃美国食物的精彩描述。

sentences.en: And it's like a Frenchman arriving in England.
sentences.zh: 就像一个法国人到了英国一样。

sentences.en: So the samurai, the head of the samurai says, the hardship cannot adequately be described by men.
sentences.zh: 武士的首领说，这种苦难简直无法用言语形容。

sentences.en: I imagine all these kind of burgers and stuff.
sentences.zh: 我能想象出那些汉堡之类的东西。

sentences.en: That terrible bacon the Americans have.
sentences.zh: 美国人那种糟糕的培根。

sentences.en: And the cheese.
sentences.zh: 还有奶酪。

sentences.en: The cheese.
sentences.zh: 奶酪。

sentences.en: Mad cheese.
sentences.zh: 疯狂的奶酪。

sentences.en: Like when you've got so many agricultural resources, why would your cheese be so pitiful?
sentences.zh: 既然你们拥有如此丰富的农业资源，为什么奶酪会做得这么可怜？

sentences.en: And don't text us about Wisconsin cheddar, because you just barely can get that.
sentences.zh: 别发信息跟我提威斯康星切达奶酪，因为你几乎买不到那种。

sentences.en: An enduring mystery, which the samurai puzzled over as well.
sentences.zh: 这是一个持久的谜团，武士们也对此感到困惑。

sentences.en: And then they get on a train and they cross the United States and they arrive in the American capital.
sentences.zh: 然后他们坐上火车横穿美国，抵达了美国首都。

sentences.en: And they're told about George Washington, first American president.
sentences.zh: 他们被告知了乔治·华盛顿，第一任美国总统的事迹。

sentences.en: And they're completely bewildered that the heirs of Washington are not in power.
sentences.zh: 他们完全无法理解为什么华盛顿的后代没有掌权。

sentences.en: So in Japan, obviously, the descendants of Tokugawa are still in power.
sentences.zh: 在日本，显然德川家族的后代依然掌握着权力。

sentences.en: So why aren't the heirs of George Washington?
sentences.zh: 所以为什么乔治·华盛顿的后代不是总统呢？

sentences.en: Why aren't they president?
sentences.zh: 为什么他们不是总统？

sentences.en: And as for the US Army, the samurai are bewildered.
sentences.zh: 至于美国军队，武士们感到困惑。

sentences.en: Because the US Army recruits people.
sentences.zh: 因为美国军队是招募士兵的。

sentences.en: So people in America are hired, not born to fight.
sentences.zh: 在美国，人们是被雇佣的，而不是生来就为了战斗。

sentences.en: And this seems to the samurai, very, very poor.
sentences.zh: 这对武士来说，显得非常、非常低劣。

sentences.en: Very, very shameful.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常可耻。

sentences.en: But of course, the attitudes that the samurai have, these medieval attitudes, if you want to frame it like that, the 19th century is coming very, very hard for them.
sentences.zh: 但当然，武士们持有的这些中世纪态度，如果你想这么定义的话，19世纪对他们来说来得非常、非常猛烈。

sentences.en: So in the early 1860s, the shogunate tries to fight back.
sentences.zh: 所以在19世纪60年代初，幕府试图反击。

sentences.en: They try and assert their dignity in the face of the American intrusion.
sentences.zh: 他们试图在面对美国入侵时维护自己的尊严。

sentences.en: I suppose a bit like the Aztecs or the Incas trying to assert their dignity in the face of the Spanish.
sentences.zh: 我想这有点像阿兹特克人或印加人试图在面对西班牙人时维护自己的尊严一样。

sentences.en: And as in South America in the 16th century, so in Japan in the 19th century, the samurai are repeatedly humiliated.
sentences.zh: 正如16世纪的南美洲一样，19世纪的日本，武士们也屡遭羞辱。

sentences.en: And of course, for a military caste to be publicly humiliated is terrible for its standing and its prestige.
sentences.zh: 当然，对于一个军事阶层来说，公开受辱对他们的地位和声望是毁灭性的。

sentences.en: So in 1866, samurai from the south of Japan repudiate the authority of the shogunate, of the Tokugawa clan.
sentences.zh: 因此在1866年，来自日本南部的武士否认了幕府，即德川家族的权威。

sentences.en: And they demand the restoration of full sovereignty to the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他们要求将全部主权归还给天皇。

sentences.en: They want the emperor to step up to the plate and stop being a kind of cipher.
sentences.zh: 他们希望天皇能够挺身而出，不再做一个傀儡。

sentences.en: And the following year, the reigning shogun resigns.
sentences.zh: 第二年，在位的将军辞职了。

sentences.en: And then in January 1868, in the imperial palace in Kyoto, the ancient capital, the restoration of rule by the emperor is officially proclaimed.
sentences.zh: 随后在1868年1月，在古都京都的皇宫里，正式宣布了天皇亲政的恢复。

sentences.en: So the house of Tokugawa at last, after 250 years, has fallen.
sentences.zh: 所以德川家族在统治250年后，终于倒台了。

sentences.en: But with the fall of the Tokugawa, you also have the fall of the samurai.
sentences.zh: 但随着德川幕府的倒台，武士阶层也随之终结。

sentences.en: So that's the Meiji restoration, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 这就是明治维新，对吧？

sentences.en: Which is seen as the sort of the transformative moment in the history of modern Japan, because
sentences.zh: 它被视为现代日本历史上的转型时刻，因为

sentences.en: it's the moment that Japan, you know, it doesn't renounce the past, but it renounces maybe to
sentences.zh: 这是日本不再摒弃过去，但也许在某种程度上摒弃了

sentences.en: some degree the cult of the stultifying cult of the past and throws itself into the pursuit of modernity.
sentences.zh: 那种令人窒息的对过去的崇拜，并投身于对现代性的追求。

sentences.en: Yeah, so there's a manifesto pledge is proclaimed in the imperial palace in April 1868.
sentences.zh: 是的，1868年4月在皇宫颁布了一份誓文。

sentences.en: And it goes, evil customs of the past shall be broken off and everything based upon the just laws of nature.
sentences.zh: 内容是：破除旧有之陋习，一切基于自然之公道。

sentences.en: And actually, what this means in practice, it is a kind of headlong rush to modernize.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这意味着一种向现代化的急速冲刺。

sentences.en: And the faster that Japan starts to westernize, obviously, the more anachronistic this kind of hereditary cast of warriors comes to seem.
sentences.zh: 日本西化的速度越快，这种世袭的武士阶层显然就显得越过时。

sentences.en: And of course, Japan modernizes incredibly effectively.
sentences.zh: 当然，日本的现代化进程非常有效。

sentences.en: I mean, more effectively, probably, than any other country that comes into contact with the industrial WeSt.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，可能比任何其他与工业化西方接触的国家都要有效。

sentences.en: And by the end of 1876, pretty much everything that had made the samurai distinctive for centuries and centuries and centuries has gone.
sentences.zh: 到1876年底，几个世纪以来使武士与众不同的几乎所有特征都消失了。

sentences.en: So their elevated kind of position in a formal hierarchy, you know, their standing as the top caste is abolished, the stipends they'd been receiving from the government.
sentences.zh: 他们在正式等级制度中的崇高地位，也就是他们作为最高阶层的地位被废除了，政府发放的俸禄也取消了。

sentences.en: They've gone.
sentences.zh: 它们消失了。

sentences.en: Their monopoly on military service, that's gone.
sentences.zh: 他们对兵役的垄断，也消失了。

sentences.en: Anyone now can join the armed services.
sentences.zh: 现在任何人都可以加入武装部队。

sentences.en: The right to wear a sword in public, the katana, that's gone as well.
sentences.zh: 在公共场合佩戴武士刀的权利，也消失了。

sentences.en: And even their distinctive hairstyle, which anyone who has seen shogun will immediately recognize, kind of the shaved front with a top knot, that's gone as well.
sentences.zh: 甚至他们独特的发型，看过《幕府将军》的人都会立刻认出来，那种剃掉前额留着发髻的发型，也消失了。

sentences.en: So it's not just the Tokugawa shogunate that's been abolished.
sentences.zh: 所以不仅仅是德川幕府被废除了。

sentences.en: So too has this entire tradition of military rule in Japan that, as we will find out, stretches way, way, way back into the Middle Ages.
sentences.zh: 日本整个军事统治的传统也随之终结，正如我们将要了解到的，这一传统可以追溯到遥远的中世纪。

sentences.en: I mean, obviously, there are people in Japan who are very sad, I suppose, who mourn the death of tradition that comes with the Meiji Restoration.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，显然日本国内有人感到非常悲伤，我想，他们哀悼随着明治维新而逝去的传统。

sentences.en: And oddly, Westerners have a very ambiguous attitude too, because on the one hand, people who like Japanese culture love it as a kind of crucible of modernity.
sentences.zh: 奇怪的是，西方人也有非常矛盾的态度，一方面，喜欢日本文化的人将其视为现代性的熔炉。

sentences.en: But we are constantly fascinated by the sort of the tradition and the reverence for the past and all of that kind of thing, which is why when you go to Japan, as I mean, we've
sentences.zh: 但我们总是被那种传统和对过去的崇敬所吸引，这就是为什么当你去日本时，正如我们

sentences.en: both done, you know, the samurai are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 两人都做过的那样，你会发现武士无处不在。

sentences.en: Katanas are everywhere.
sentences.zh: 武士刀无处不在。

sentences.en: I mean, I have to say Sambra Jr.
sentences.zh: 我必须说，小桑布拉

sentences.en: returned with an excellent sword and all kinds of samurai gear from Japan.
sentences.zh: 从日本带回了一把极好的剑和各种武士装备。

sentences.en: There are definitely people in the West who mourn the collapse of the samurai, even though, of course, you know, it's the West that has precipitated their downfall.
sentences.zh: 西方确实有人哀悼武士的崩溃，尽管当然，正是西方加速了他们的灭亡。

sentences.en: And I think what they particularly admire and regret is a kind of aesthetic.
sentences.zh: 我认为他们特别钦佩和怀念的是一种美学。

sentences.en: It's the look that the samurai have.
sentences.zh: 那是武士的外观。

sentences.en: And so, for instance, you know, these suits of armor that will be familiar in the West that you get in museums, say British Museum or wherever.
sentences.zh: 例如，西方人熟悉的那些在博物馆里能看到的盔甲，比如大英博物馆或其他地方。

sentences.en: These are sold by ex-samurai because every samurai had to have a suit of armor.
sentences.zh: 这些都是前武士出售的，因为每个武士都必须有一套盔甲。

sentences.en: They don't need them anymore.
sentences.zh: 他们不再需要它们了。

sentences.en: They're a bit short of money.
sentences.zh: 他们手头有点紧。

sentences.en: Now they're not getting their stipends.
sentences.zh: 现在他们拿不到俸禄了。

sentences.en: So they flog them off.
sentences.zh: 所以他们把它们卖掉了。

sentences.en: And so they go around the world and they kind of broadcast the look of the samurai across the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 于是它们流向世界各地，将武士的形象传播到整个西方。

sentences.en: And helmets in particular become kind of icons of what in France is known as a Japanese,
sentences.zh: 头盔尤其成为了法国所称的“日本主义”的标志，

sentences.en: which is kind of the craze for Japanese art, Japanese fashion, Japanese vibes that completely sweeps Western Europe in the 19th century.
sentences.zh: 这是一种在19世纪席卷西欧的对日本艺术、时尚和氛围的狂热。

sentences.en: And they remain absolutely iconic to this day.
sentences.zh: 它们至今仍是绝对的标志性符号。

sentences.en: And they're instant signifiers of medieval Japan, even though often, of course, they come from the 16th or 17th centuries.
sentences.zh: 它们是中世纪日本的即时象征，尽管当然，它们通常来自16世纪或17世纪。

sentences.en: And you talked about a very, very celebrated marker of that influence, which endures into the present day.
sentences.zh: 你谈到了这种影响的一个非常、非常著名的标志，它一直延续到今天。

sentences.en: And it's there in the British Museum show because you begin with this stunning suit of armor, which I described.
sentences.zh: 在大英博物馆的展览中就有体现，因为展览以我描述的那套精美盔甲开始。

sentences.en: You go around the show and then at the end, you have an outfit that deliberately echoed the suit of armor that you got at the beginning.
sentences.zh: 你参观完展览，最后会看到一套刻意呼应开头那套盔甲的服装。

sentences.zh: 这位军阀名叫平将门。

sentences.en: And he is a remarkable man of whom remarkable things are reported.
sentences.zh: 他是一个非凡的人，关于他有许多非凡的传闻。

sentences.en: So, first of all, he's an absolute unit.
sentences.zh: 首先，他是一个绝对的庞然大物。

sentences.en: He is seven foot tall.
sentences.zh: 他身高七英尺。

sentences.en: And the Japanese are not at all people.
sentences.zh: 而日本人根本不是那样的人。

sentences.en: So, he really stands out.
sentences.zh: 所以，他真的很显眼。

sentences.en: In his left eye, he has two pupils, which again, unusual.
sentences.zh: 他的左眼有两个瞳孔，这同样很不寻常。

sentences.en: That is unusual.
sentences.zh: 那确实很不寻常。

sentences.en: Indeed, unheard of.
sentences.zh: 确实，闻所未闻。

sentences.en: But perhaps the most striking thing about him is he is completely invulnerable to weapons.
sentences.zh: 但关于他最引人注目的地方也许是他对武器完全免疫。

sentences.en: And this is thanks to his mother, who was a giant snake.
sentences.zh: 这要归功于他的母亲，她是一条巨蛇。

sentences.en: And I gather it's the custom for giant snakes to lick their offspring.
sentences.zh: 我了解到巨蛇舔舐后代是习俗。

sentences.en: And so, his mother, the giant snake, had licked Masakado all over, with the exception of his forehead.
sentences.zh: 所以，他的母亲，那条巨蛇，舔遍了将门的全身，除了他的前额。

sentences.en: And her saliva had the magical power of making him invulnerable to weapons.
sentences.zh: 她的唾液有一种神奇的力量，使他能够对武器免疫。

sentences.en: So, there's a slight hint there of Achilles.
sentences.zh: 所以，这里有一点阿喀琉斯的影子。

sentences.en: Two pupils.
sentences.zh: 两个瞳孔。

sentences.en: That's weird.
sentences.zh: 那太奇怪了。

sentences.en: Anyway, what happens to the head?
sentences.zh: 总之，那个头颅发生了什么？

sentences.en: What do they do with it?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么处理它？

sentences.en: So, the head is exhibited in the marketplace of Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 那个头颅被陈列在京都的市场上。

sentences.en: So, there's a spike.
sentences.zh: 所以，有一根长矛。

sentences.en: They put the head on the spike.
sentences.zh: 他们把头颅插在长矛上。

sentences.en: And they lift the pole up so that the head is gazing out over the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 他们把杆子竖起来，让头颅俯瞰着市场。

sentences.en: And the moment the pole has been levered into position, the eye is open, complete with the left eye with its two pupils.
sentences.zh: 当杆子被撬到位置的那一刻，眼睛睁开了，包括那只带有两个瞳孔的左眼。

sentences.en: And they glare around angrily.
sentences.zh: 它们愤怒地四处瞪视。

sentences.en: And the head demands to know where the rest of the body is.
sentences.zh: 头颅要求知道身体的其他部分在哪里。

sentences.en: So, very annoyed that the body parts have gone missing.
sentences.zh: 所以，它对身体部位的丢失感到非常恼火。

sentences.en: And it stays there for several months.
sentences.zh: 它在那里待了好几个月。

sentences.en: And all this time, it doesn't rot in the slighteSt.
sentences.zh: 在这段时间里，它一点也没有腐烂。

sentences.en: It's silent for periods.
sentences.zh: 它有时会保持沉默。

sentences.en: And then it has another massive rant demanding its legs back and its arms and so on.
sentences.zh: 然后它又会进行另一次大规模的咆哮，要求找回它的腿、手臂等等。

sentences.en: And then, after several months, it suddenly starts to glow.
sentences.zh: 然后，几个月后，它突然开始发光。

sentences.en: And then it shoots up off the spike.
sentences.zh: 接着它从长矛上弹射而起。

sentences.en: And it goes bombing off across Kyoto in search of its decapitated corpse.
sentences.zh: 它在京都上空飞驰，寻找它被斩首的尸体。

sentences.en: And it heads eastwards across this great mountain range, which separates Kyoto from Kanto, which is the Great Plain to the eaSt.
sentences.zh: 它向东飞越了将京都与关东隔开的巨大山脉，关东就是东部的大平原。

sentences.en: And as it's flying over Kanto, this head is brought down, either because it gets shot down by a god.
sentences.zh: 当它飞越关东时，这个头颅被击落了，要么是因为它被一位神射了下来。

sentences.en: That's according to one account.
sentences.zh: 这是根据一种说法。

sentences.en: Or because it crash lands for reasons that aren't explained.
sentences.zh: 要么是因为它因无法解释的原因坠毁了。

sentences.en: But whatever, the head crash lands and locals go and pick it up and they wash it and they bury it and they raise a mound over it.
sentences.zh: 但无论如何，头颅坠毁了，当地人去捡起它，清洗它，埋葬它，并在上面筑起了一座土丘。

sentences.en: And, of course, this is regarded as a very sacred place.
sentences.zh: 当然，这被认为是一个非常神圣的地方。

sentences.en: And people go to Tokyo today, you can still see it.
sentences.zh: 今天人们去东京，仍然可以看到它。

sentences.en: This mound, the tomb of Mascado's head, because it stands right in the middle of Tokyo's business district, among the most valuable real estate in the entire world.
sentences.zh: 这个土丘，将门首级的坟墓，因为它就矗立在东京商业区的中心，位于世界上最昂贵的房地产之中。

sentences.en: So you would think, well, surely this has been cleared, surely they built some skyscraper or something.
sentences.zh: 所以你会想，好吧，这肯定已经被清理过了，他们肯定盖了什么摩天大楼之类的。

sentences.en: But they haven't, because every attempt to build on it has resulted in disaster.
sentences.zh: 但他们没有，因为每一次在上面建造的尝试都导致了灾难。

sentences.en: So, you know, they might lift up a crane and the crane comes crashing down.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，他们可能会升起一台起重机，起重机就会坠毁。

sentences.en: Or the head of the company that is trying to develop it kind of gets run over by a car or something.
sentences.zh: 或者试图开发它的公司老板会被车撞倒之类的。

sentences.en: And so the Japanese in Tokyo have drawn the lesson that you shouldn't try and erase the last resting place of Mascado's head.
sentences.zh: 所以东京的日本人得出的教训是，你不应该试图抹去将门首级的最后安息之地。

sentences.en: And so his tomb stands there to this day.
sentences.zh: 所以他的墓至今仍矗立在那里。

sentences.en: This is because he's the first samurai, right?
sentences.zh: 这是因为他是第一位武士，对吧？

sentences.en: So you can't mess with the first samurai.
sentences.zh: 所以你不能招惹第一位武士。

sentences.en: And he's the guy who, he's the founding father of this tradition that we're talking about in this series.
sentences.zh: 他就是我们这个系列所探讨的这一传统的开创者。

sentences.en: Correct.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So Mascado is essentially, he's kind of fated as the first samurai.
sentences.zh: 所以将门基本上被视为第一位武士。

sentences.en: And that is absolutely why he has this kind of resonance, this mythic status.
sentences.zh: 这绝对是他为何具有这种影响力、这种神话地位的原因。

sentences.en: So obviously, there's quite a lot to pick here.
sentences.zh: 显然，这里有很多值得深究的地方。

sentences.en: So again, because geography is really important in this story,
sentences.zh: 再次强调，因为地理位置在这个故事中非常重要，

sentences.en: let's just look at how the geography of Japan maps onto the kind of the politics of the empire in the mid-10th century.
sentences.zh: 让我们来看看日本的地理是如何映射到10世纪中叶帝国政治格局上的。

sentences.en: Because this is essentially what the story is illustrating, the political geography of Japan.
sentences.zh: 因为这基本上就是这个故事所展示的内容，即日本的政治地理。

sentences.en: So Mascado's head has been brought from the plain of Kanto, which literally means east of the kind of the mountain range, east of the barrier.
sentences.zh: 将门的首级是从关东平原送来的，关东字面意思就是山脉以东，关卡以东。

sentences.en: And it's been brought to Kyoto because Kyoto is, it's not just the great center of power.
sentences.zh: 它被送到京都，因为京都不仅仅是伟大的权力中心。

sentences.en: It's the only center of power in the Japanese archipelago in this period.
sentences.zh: 它是那个时期日本列岛唯一的权力中心。

sentences.en: And it's been founded in 794.
sentences.zh: 它始建于794年。

sentences.en: It's the seat of the Japanese emperor.
sentences.zh: 它是日本天皇的驻地。

sentences.en: And the emperor rules as a lineal descendant of the sun goddess.
sentences.zh: 天皇作为太阳女神的直系后裔进行统治。

sentences.en: And then a succession of 15 emperors who, between them, were supposed to have ruled for centuries and centuries and centuries.
sentences.zh: 还有历代15位天皇，他们加起来据称统治了数百年之久。

sentences.en: So they're a bit like the kind of the biblical prophets.
sentences.zh: 所以他们有点像圣经里的先知。

sentences.en: They have improbable lifespans.
sentences.zh: 他们有着不可思议的寿命。

sentences.en: So that's the story that's told.
sentences.zh: 这就是流传的故事。

sentences.en: The reality is rather different.
sentences.zh: 但现实却大相径庭。

sentences.en: What becomes the Japanese imperial dynasty had originally been just one of a number of competing kind of aristocratic families.
sentences.zh: 后来成为日本皇室的家族，最初只是众多相互竞争的贵族家庭之一。

sentences.en: And it's only at the end of the 7th century that it succeeds in establishing its overall supremacy and with it, its imperial status.
sentences.zh: 直到7世纪末，它才成功确立了整体的统治地位，并随之确立了其皇室地位。

sentences.en: And then having established the supremacy, of course, it faces the challenge of maintaining it.
sentences.zh: 当然，在确立了统治地位之后，它面临着维持这种地位的挑战。

sentences.en: How are they going to do that?
sentences.zh: 他们打算怎么做呢？

sentences.en: And initially, they do this in a kind of classic way.
sentences.zh: 起初，他们以一种经典的方式来做。

sentences.en: By establishing a monopoly of violence.
sentences.zh: 通过建立对暴力的垄断。

sentences.en: That's what imperial regimes invariably do.
sentences.zh: 这是帝国政权总是会做的事情。

sentences.en: So the emperor requires all the other lords to hand over their military equipment, their crossbows and so on.
sentences.zh: 所以天皇要求所有其他领主上交他们的军事装备，比如弩等等。

sentences.en: And these are confiscated and put in regional depots that are dotted around the empire so that they can be drawn on in case of emergency.
sentences.zh: 这些武器被没收并存放在帝国各地零星分布的仓库中，以便在紧急情况下调用。

sentences.en: See, this is a period when the Japanese are sedulously imitating China, which is the great model for them.
sentences.zh: 你看，这是一个日本人勤奋模仿中国的时期，中国是他们伟大的榜样。

sentences.en: And in China, the army consists of a great mass of conscripted peasants.
sentences.zh: 在中国，军队由大量的征召农民组成。

sentences.en: And so the Japanese emperor does the same.
sentences.zh: 所以日本天皇也照做了。

sentences.en: This is going to provide him with his manpower.
sentences.zh: 这将为他提供兵源。

sentences.en: But it doesn't really work in the Japanese context.
sentences.zh: 但在日本的背景下，这并不奏效。

sentences.en: And that's partly because there are far fewer peasants in Japan than there are in China.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是日本的农民远比中国少。

sentences.en: So peasants don't really provide the emperor with the kind of military mass that he needs.
sentences.zh: 所以农民并不能为天皇提供他所需要的军事规模。

sentences.en: But it's also because there is a massive fiscal crisis and it becomes too expensive for the emperor to run his own army.
sentences.zh: 但这也是因为当时存在严重的财政危机，天皇维持自己的军队变得太昂贵了。

sentences.en: And also peasants just make terrible soldiers.
sentences.zh: 而且农民本身就是糟糕的士兵。

sentences.en: They're hopeless.
sentences.zh: 他们毫无用处。

sentences.en: They're always kind of running away and stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们总是逃跑之类的。

sentences.en: But just what do they need the soldiers for?
sentences.zh: 但他们到底需要士兵做什么呢？

sentences.en: Because who are they fighting?
sentences.zh: 因为他们在和谁打仗？

sentences.en: They're not going to be attacked by external enemies.
sentences.zh: 他们不会受到外部敌人的攻击。

sentences.en: Are they China, Korea or whoever?
sentences.zh: 是中国、朝鲜还是其他什么人？

sentences.en: So what do they, is it internal threats?
sentences.zh: 所以他们，这是内部威胁吗？

sentences.en: By this point, the southwestern half of Japan has basically been pacified.
sentences.zh: 到这个时候，日本的西南部基本上已经被平定了。

sentences.en: So that would include Kushu, which is the kind of southwestern island.
sentences.zh: 这包括九州，也就是那个西南部的岛屿。

sentences.en: And then you have the main island, Honshu, up to this kind of great range of mountains east of Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 然后是主岛本州，一直到京都以东的那片大山脉。

sentences.en: All of these have been pacified.
sentences.zh: 所有这些地方都已被平定。

sentences.en: And so you don't really need an army in that kind of southwestern half of Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以你在日本的西南部确实不需要军队。

sentences.en: Because effectively, it's fine to have civilian government there.
sentences.zh: 因为实际上，在那里实行文官政府就可以了。

sentences.en: And all the regional aristocracy by now are obsessed by hanging out in Kyoto, in this great capital.
sentences.zh: 而且所有的地区贵族现在都沉迷于在京都这个大首都里消磨时光。

sentences.en: And they go there and they kind of write poetry and they practice calligraphy and they mix incense.
sentences.zh: 他们去那里写诗、练习书法、调配香料。

sentences.en: And this is how you prove your status, not by going out and fighting.
sentences.zh: 这就是你证明自己地位的方式，而不是通过外出打仗。

sentences.en: And actually, it's quite like Versailles in the 18th century.
sentences.zh: 实际上，这很像18世纪的凡尔赛宫。

sentences.en: Lords do not want to stay in the provinces.
sentences.zh: 领主们不想待在地方上。

sentences.en: They want to go to the court.
sentences.zh: 他们想去宫廷。

sentences.en: They want to show off there.
sentences.zh: 他们想在那里炫耀。

sentences.en: They want to adopt the arts of peace.
sentences.zh: 他们想学习和平的艺术。

sentences.en: And so warriors, as the centuries pass, come to seem to the court, they're uncouth, they're murderous.
sentences.zh: 因此，随着世纪流逝，武士在宫廷眼中变得粗野、嗜杀。

sentences.en: Basically, they're scum.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们就是渣滓。

sentences.en: They're kind of literally described as dogs.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至被直接描述为狗。

sentences.en: War has become something that is vulgar.
sentences.zh: 战争已经变得庸俗。

sentences.en: It's become something de classe.
sentences.zh: 它变得格调低下。

sentences.en: It's something that no one with any standing or status would dream of doing.
sentences.zh: 这是任何有地位或身份的人都不会想做的事情。

sentences.en: And yet, you might say that any regime that has a contempt or disregard for military muscle is living on borrowed time, because that's what power is all about.
sentences.zh: 然而，你可能会说，任何蔑视或忽视军事力量的政权都是在苟延残喘，因为权力归根结底就是这么回事。

sentences.en: So presumably, they don't ignore military muscle completely.
sentences.zh: 所以大概他们并没有完全忽视军事力量？

sentences.en: Well, no, because we've said the northeastern reaches of Honshu, this main island of Japan, that remains un-pacified.
sentences.zh: 嗯，没有，因为我们说过本州岛（日本主岛）的东北部地区尚未被平定。

sentences.en: And so the provinces beyond the mountains east of Kyoto have this kind of real marcher feel.
sentences.zh: 所以京都以东山脉之外的省份有一种真正的边疆感。

sentences.en: You know, they are kind of frontier zone.
sentences.zh: 你知道，它们属于边境地带。

sentences.en: And here, the imperial government has no option but to reverse its previous policy and to encourage the governors, the lords who live in these northeastern provinces,
sentences.zh: 在这里，帝国政府别无选择，只能扭转之前的政策，鼓励这些东北省份的知事和领主们，

sentences.en: to levy their own troops, because they need them to keep order there.
sentences.zh: 征募他们自己的军队，因为他们需要这些人来维持当地的秩序。

sentences.en: And so who are these troops?
sentences.zh: 那么这些军队是什么人呢？

sentences.en: Well, these lords are still kind of emulating the Chinese model and recruiting peasants who serve them as infantry.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这些领主仍然在效仿中国模式，招募农民作为步兵为他们服务。

sentences.en: But there's the same problem.
sentences.zh: 但问题依然存在。

sentences.en: The peasants are rubbish.
sentences.zh: 农民们很差劲。

sentences.en: They're always running away and throwing away their weapons and things.
sentences.zh: 他们总是逃跑、丢弃武器之类的。

sentences.en: And so the key figures, the key players, as in medieval Europe, are horsemen.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如中世纪欧洲一样，关键人物、关键角色是骑兵。

sentences.en: And these are called suwamono.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为“兵”（suwamono）。

sentences.en: And these are warriors who were trained from childhood to shoot arrows from the saddle.
sentences.zh: 这些武士从小就接受在马背上射箭的训练。

sentences.en: So in that sense, they are like the kind of the classical horsemen of the steppes, you know, the Mongols included.
sentences.zh: 从这个意义上说，他们就像草原上的古典骑兵，你知道，包括蒙古人在内。

sentences.en: And the great obsession of these horsemen in northeastern Japan is honor.
sentences.zh: 这些日本东北部骑兵最大的执念是荣誉。

sentences.en: And the great fear is disgrace, which isn't to say that they're not also very, very obsessed by financial rewards and other rewards as well, because they are.
sentences.zh: 最大的恐惧是耻辱，这并不是说他们不也非常、非常执着于经济回报和其他奖励，因为他们确实如此。

sentences.en: And it's this kind of fusion of obsessional interest in their own honor and an obsessional interest in getting on in life that makes them, you know, if you want a samurai code,
sentences.zh: 正是这种对自身荣誉的执着追求与对人生进取的执着追求的融合，使得他们——如果你想要一个武士准则的话，

sentences.en: that is the samurai code.
sentences.zh: 这就是武士准则。

sentences.en: They are called samurai because they are the retainers who are recruited by the local lords to serve him as his muscle, you know, as his kind of backup.
sentences.zh: 他们被称为武士，因为他们是当地领主招募的家臣，作为他的武力，你知道，作为他的后盾。

sentences.en: You might say, so as a layman, I might say that's very risky, because basically, if local magnates are recruiting their own troops to fight off, you know,
sentences.zh: 你可能会说，作为一个外行，我会说这风险很大，因为基本上，如果地方豪强招募自己的军队来抵御，你知道，

sentences.en: the barbarians or whatever, then, you know, the lesson of late Roman history is when there are, you know,
sentences.zh: 蛮族什么的，那么，你知道，罗马帝国晚期的教训就是，当有，你知道，

sentences.en: it won't be long before one of them declares himself emperor and marches on the capital.
sentences.zh: 用不了多久，其中一个人就会自立为帝并向首都进军。

sentences.en: No?
sentences.zh: 不是吗？

sentences.en: In the long run, as we will see, you are not wrong.
sentences.zh: 从长远来看，正如我们将看到的，你并没有说错。

sentences.en: And this is obviously going to be a problem, but not immediately.
sentences.zh: 这显然会成为一个问题，但不会立即发生。

sentences.en: And this is for various reasons.
sentences.zh: 这有各种各样的原因。

sentences.en: And the first is that these provincial governors to the northeast of the great mountain range that separates Kyoto from the northeast of Honshu, they all hate each other.
sentences.zh: 首先，这些位于将京都与本州东北部隔开的大山脉东北侧的地方知事，他们彼此都非常憎恨。

sentences.en: So it's very, very unlikely that they're going to gang up and kind of march on Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 所以他们联合起来向京都进军的可能性非常、非常小。

sentences.en: And if there is a rebellion, then it's very easy for the imperial government to find someone on the scene who's going to crush it, because Kyoto is the source of all patronage.
sentences.zh: 如果发生叛乱，帝国政府很容易在现场找到人来镇压它，因为京都是一切恩惠的来源。

sentences.en: And so all you have to do is say, well, you know, I'll send you a nice calligraphy kit, go and beat up this guy and the guy will do it.
sentences.zh: 所以你只需要说，嗯，你知道，我会送你一套精美的书法工具，去把这家伙打一顿，那个人就会照做。

sentences.en: And again, there's this whole Versailles thing, because even provincial governors out in the sticks, you know, they buy into the notion of what is fashionable,
sentences.zh: 同样，这里也有凡尔赛的那一套，因为即使是偏远地区的地方知事，你知道，他们也认同什么是时尚，

sentences.en: of what gives them status, which is the kind of the ideals of a centralized court running everything.
sentences.zh: 什么能赋予他们地位，那就是由中央朝廷统管一切的理想。

sentences.en: And Kyoto provides the only standard by which even people out in, you know, the northeast of Honshu want to be judged.
sentences.zh: 京都提供了唯一的标准，即使是本州东北部的人也希望以此来衡量自己。

sentences.en: And it's the only source of the lifestyle that ultimately matters, the lifestyle that gives you status.
sentences.zh: 它是最终重要的生活方式的唯一来源，那种赋予你地位的生活方式。

sentences.en: And Carl Friday, great scholar of early medieval Japan, he compares these governors, these warlords in the northeast of Honshu with CEOs today.
sentences.zh: 日本中世纪早期伟大的学者卡尔·弗莱迪（Carl Friday）将这些本州东北部的知事、军阀与今天的首席执行官们进行了比较。

sentences.en: And so to quote Friday, who tend to identify more closely with CEOs in other lines of business than with the workers, engineers or middle managers in their own.
sentences.zh: 引用弗莱迪的话，他们往往比认同自己公司里的工人、工程师或中层管理人员，更认同其他行业的首席执行官。

sentences.en: So it's like, you know, tech CEOs, industrial CEOs, financial CEOs going to Davos.
sentences.zh: 所以这就像，你知道，科技公司CEO、工业CEO、金融CEO去参加达沃斯论坛一样。

sentences.en: They have more in common with each other than they do with the kind of the minions far below them in their kind of various corporate structures.
sentences.zh: 他们彼此之间的共同点，比他们与各自公司结构中远在下层的下属之间的共同点要多得多。

sentences.en: So in other words, you know, in the Japanese context, just because you employ mercenaries doesn't mean that you want to be a mercenary yourself.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，你知道，在日本的背景下，仅仅因为你雇佣了雇佣兵，并不意味着你自己想成为雇佣兵。

sentences.en: You know, you want to keep them at a kind of distance.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你想和他们保持一定的距离。

sentences.en: And they are related to the emperors by and large, aren't they?
sentences.zh: 他们大体上都和天皇有亲戚关系，不是吗？

sentences.en: They're from the imperial family, most of these governors?
sentences.zh: 这些知事大多数都来自皇室？

sentences.en: Yeah, so that's a third factor that is kind of reigning in displays of military Bracadaccio that are not sanctioned by the court.
sentences.zh: 是的，这是第三个因素，它在某种程度上抑制了那些未经朝廷批准的军事炫耀行为。

sentences.en: So regular listeners to the rest of history may recall that this is not the first series that we've done on imperial Japan.
sentences.zh: 所以《历史的其余部分》的常客可能还记得，这不是我们制作的关于日本帝国的第一部系列节目。

sentences.en: Because last year, we did a couple of episodes on the great female writers at the imperial Japanese court around the year 1000.
sentences.zh: 因为去年，我们制作了几集关于公元1000年左右日本皇室宫廷中伟大女性作家的节目。

sentences.en: And the first of these episodes was on the tale of Genji, which is an enormous 1100 page novel written around the year 1000 by Murasaki Shikibu, Lady Murasaki,
sentences.zh: 这些剧集的第一集是关于《源氏物语》，这是一部由紫式部（Lady Murasaki）在公元1000年左右写成的长达1100页的巨著，

sentences.en: and set in the imperial court.
sentences.zh: 故事背景设定在皇室宫廷中。

sentences.en: And the hero of that novel was the son of an emperor by one of his concubines.
sentences.zh: 这部小说的男主角是天皇与其中一位妃子所生的儿子。

sentences.en: And because he's the son of a concubine, he has no prospect of inheriting the throne.
sentences.zh: 因为他是妃子所生，他没有继承皇位的希望。

sentences.en: And so his father, the emperor, is keen for this boy, who he recognizes as being very talented, to have a career of public service,
sentences.zh: 所以他的父亲，天皇，很希望这个被他认为非常有才华的男孩能从事公共服务事业，

sentences.en: rather than kind of hanging around in the palace, being a drone, doing nothing.
sentences.zh: 而不是在宫里游手好闲，当个无所事事的寄生虫。

sentences.en: And so he takes this very drastic step.
sentences.zh: 于是他采取了一个非常激进的步骤。

sentences.en: He removes the boy from the imperial family by giving him what no emperor ever has, namely a surname.
sentences.zh: 他通过给予他前所未有的东西，即一个姓氏，将这个男孩从皇室中除名。

sentences.en: So this young prince, it's not seen as, you know, he's not being disgraced.
sentences.zh: 所以这个年轻的王子，这并不被视为，你知道，他并没有蒙羞。

sentences.en: It's not because he's misbehaved.
sentences.zh: 这不是因为他行为不端。

sentences.en: It's actually the opposite.
sentences.zh: 事实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: It's because his father recognizes in him great talents and doesn't want them to atrophy, doesn't want them to go to waste.
sentences.zh: 这是因为他的父亲在他身上看到了伟大的才华，不想让这些才华萎缩，不想让它们被浪费。

sentences.en: He wants this boy to go out and kind of, you know, make something of his life.
sentences.zh: 他希望这个男孩走出去，你知道，成就一番事业。

sentences.en: And so, as you said, the surname this boy is given is Genji.
sentences.zh: 所以，正如你所说，这个男孩被赐予的姓氏是源氏（Genji）。

sentences.en: And as a Genji, he belongs to two realMs.
sentences.zh: 作为源氏，他属于两个领域。

sentences.en: He belongs to the realm of his father, the realm of the imperial family, but also the realm of the nobility of the great kind of public figures who serve the palace.
sentences.zh: 他属于他父亲的领域，即皇室领域，但也属于贵族领域，即服务于宫廷的伟大公众人物的领域。

sentences.en: And Lady Murasaki, when she was writing the tale of Genji in the year 1000, was writing it as a historical novel.
sentences.zh: 紫式部在公元1000年写《源氏物语》时，是把它作为历史小说来写的。

sentences.en: So she is casting Genji, her hero, as the first prince to be de-princed, if you like, you know, to lose his kind of princely standing.
sentences.zh: 所以她把她的英雄源氏塑造成了第一位被“去王子化”的王子，如果你愿意这么说的话，你知道，失去了他那种王子的地位。

sentences.en: But as she well knew, Genji was not the only one, because this is a process that carries on throughout the 10th century.
sentences.zh: 但她很清楚，源氏并不是唯一一个，因为这是一个贯穿整个10世纪的过程。

sentences.en: And this is because emperors in Kyoto have multitudes of wives and concubines.
sentences.zh: 这是因为京都的天皇有众多的妻子和妃子。

sentences.en: And as a result, they have kind of vast progenies.
sentences.zh: 结果，他们有大量的后代。

sentences.en: And even by the 9th century, there are simply too many princes in the imperial system to handle.
sentences.zh: 即使到了9世纪，皇室系统里的王子也实在太多了，难以处理。

sentences.en: So even, you know, even with our own beloved royal family, this is an issue.
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，即使是我们自己深受爱戴的王室，这也是一个问题。

sentences.en: You start, you know, you accumulate princely clutter and you have to get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 你开始，你知道，积累了过多的王子，你必须摆脱他们。

sentences.en: I mean, we've discovered that two is too many, basically.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们已经发现，基本上两个就太多了。

sentences.en: Basically, pretty much.
sentences.zh: 基本上，差不多吧。

sentences.en: And in Kyoto, in the 9th and 10th century, this is even more of a problem.
sentences.zh: 而在9世纪和10世纪的京都，这个问题甚至更严重。

sentences.en: And, you know, these princes clutter up the place and they're very expensive.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这些王子把地方挤满了，而且他们非常昂贵。

sentences.en: So you've got to get rid of them.
sentences.zh: 所以你必须摆脱他们。

sentences.en: And so the solution is to cut them loose from the imperial family by giving them this special surname.
sentences.zh: 所以解决方案是通过给他们这个特殊的姓氏，将他们从皇室中剥离出来。

sentences.en: And one of these, as in Lady Murasaki's novel, is Genji, or as the clan name is more generally known, Minamoto, which is, it means origin.
sentences.zh: 其中一个，正如紫式部小说中的那样，是源氏（Genji），或者更通俗的氏族名称是平氏（Minamoto），意思是起源。

sentences.en: So Genji and Minamoto are basically the same word.
sentences.zh: 所以源氏（Genji）和源氏（Minamoto）基本上是同一个词。

sentences.en: The other dynasty is the Heike, or as it's more generally known, the Taira, which means peace.
sentences.zh: 另一个王朝是平家（Heike），或者更通俗地称为平氏（Taira），意思是和平。

sentences.en: So by the 10th century, these two clans of ex-princes, the Minamoto and the Taira, have emerged to become two of the greatest dynasties in the empire.
sentences.zh: 所以到了10世纪，这两个前王子氏族，源氏和平氏，已经崛起成为帝国最伟大的两个王朝。

sentences.en: And the field of their operations tends to lie in the provinces, and particularly the northeastern provinces in Canto and beyond Canto.
sentences.zh: 他们的活动领域往往在地方省份，特别是关东及关东以外的东北省份。

sentences.en: And here, they are very, very glamorous figures because they come trailing clouds of imperial glamour.
sentences.zh: 在这里，他们是非常、非常迷人的人物，因为他们带着皇室光环而来。

sentences.en: And they bring with them all kinds of benefits that people out in the wilds can, you know, immediately want.
sentences.zh: 他们带来了各种各样的利益，而身处荒野的人们，你知道，会立刻想要这些东西。

sentences.en: So they can offer kind of high-ranking governorships and military commands.
sentences.zh: 所以他们可以提供某种高级总督职位和军事指挥权。

sentences.en: They can offer the local aristocracy's marriage into what is a kind of, you know, it gives them a kind of imperial link.
sentences.zh: 他们可以提供与当地贵族联姻的机会，这给了他们一种皇室纽带。

sentences.en: And so lots of these regional dynasties are very, very happy to take on the name of Minamoto or Taira because they're much more glamorous than their own.
sentences.zh: 因此，许多地区性王朝非常、非常乐意冠上源氏或平氏的姓氏，因为这些姓氏比他们自己的要显赫得多。

sentences.en: And so the Minamoto and the Taira become larger and larger as kind of dynastic organizations.
sentences.zh: 于是，源氏和平氏作为王朝组织变得越来越庞大。

sentences.en: And they provide people out in the provinces with this sense that they have a real kind of a very glamorous link to what is going on in Kyoto, what is going on in the capital.
sentences.zh: 他们让偏远省份的人们感到，自己与京都、与首都正在发生的事情有着某种非常显赫的真实联系。

sentences.en: So all this is looking great.
sentences.zh: 所以这一切看起来都很棒。

sentences.en: It's all seems fine.
sentences.zh: 一切似乎都很好。

sentences.en: It's all ticking along.
sentences.zh: 一切都在按部就班地进行。

sentences.en: But as you implied, Dominic, there is a kind of potential problem here.
sentences.zh: 但正如你所暗示的，多米尼克，这里存在一种潜在的问题。

sentences.en: Because what if a Minamoto or a Taira out in the provinces should start to feel that, you know, his nose is being put out of joint, perhaps by the court in Kyoto,
sentences.zh: 因为如果身处省份的源氏或平氏成员开始觉得，你知道，他的利益受到了损害，也许是京都的朝廷所为，

sentences.en: perhaps by another member of his clan, perhaps by both.
sentences.zh: 也许是他的氏族成员所为，也许两者皆有。

sentences.en: You know, they have warriors at their back.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们背后有武士撑腰。

sentences.en: What is to stop them going a little bit rogue?
sentences.zh: 有什么能阻止他们变得有点无法无天呢？

sentences.en: And this, in the 930s, is precisely how Taira no Massacado, so he is the first samurai, the guy whose head goes flying off after it's been decapitated.
sentences.zh: 在930年代，这正是平将门的情况，他是第一位武士，就是那个被斩首后头颅飞走的人。

sentences.en: This is how he comes to feel.
sentences.zh: 他就是这样想的。

sentences.en: Because he is a Taira, right?
sentences.zh: 因为他是平氏，对吧？

sentences.en: He's from the Taira clan.
sentences.zh: 他来自平氏家族。

sentences.en: Yes, he is.
sentences.zh: 是的，他是。

sentences.en: And so he is of imperial descent.
sentences.zh: 所以他拥有皇室血统。

sentences.en: But he is very bitterly conscious of being kind of downwardly mobile.
sentences.zh: 但他非常痛苦地意识到自己正在走下坡路。

sentences.en: Things are not going well for him.
sentences.zh: 他的境况并不好。

sentences.en: So he had been born in the northern reaches of Kanto, this kind of great plain beyond the mountains that separate it from Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 他出生在关东的北部地区，那是群山之外的一片大平原，将它与京都隔离开来。

sentences.en: And he has grown up a very formidable warrior.
sentences.zh: 他成长为一名非常强大的武士。

sentences.en: And as we said, he's an absolute unit, absolutely huge.
sentences.zh: 正如我们所说，他是个绝对的猛男，体格极其魁梧。

sentences.en: He's got his two eyeballs in his left eye.
sentences.zh: 他的左眼长着两个眼珠。

sentences.en: And he has made himself a master of what is described by the samurai as the way of the bow and the horse.
sentences.zh: 他使自己成为了武士所描述的“弓马之道”的大师。

sentences.en: In other words, he's a great horseman, and he can fire a bow sitting in the saddle.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，他是一位伟大的骑手，能在马鞍上开弓射箭。

sentences.en: It's not enough for Minamoto just to be a warrior, because that would mean that he really has kind of gone down socially.
sentences.zh: 对于源氏来说，仅仅做一个武士是不够的，因为那意味着他在社会地位上确实下降了。

sentences.en: He's kind of lost his status.
sentences.zh: 他算是失去了自己的地位。

sentences.en: He wants to be doing his calligraphy and his poetry and stuff as well, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 他也想做书法、诗歌之类的事情，不是吗？

sentences.en: Kind of.
sentences.zh: 算是吧。

sentences.en: I think by this point, I think he's less interested in that.
sentences.zh: 我想到了这一点，我觉得他对此兴趣不大。

sentences.en: But he wants the kind of the stamp of authority and glamour that only the imperial court ultimately can provide.
sentences.zh: 但他想要那种最终只有皇室才能提供的权威和光环的印记。

sentences.en: And so he applies for a government post, a post that will say to everyone around him, yes, I have imperial favor.
sentences.zh: 所以他申请了一个政府职位，一个能向周围所有人宣告“是的，我拥有皇室恩宠”的职位。

sentences.en: And he gets turned down.
sentences.zh: 结果他被拒绝了。

sentences.en: And then he is snubbed by his own uncle, a guy called Taira Yoshikane.
sentences.zh: 然后他又被自己的叔叔，一个叫平良兼的人冷落了。

sentences.en: And what Mascado has done is to ask Yoshikane, his uncle, for his daughter, so his cousin, to be his wife.
sentences.zh: 将门所做的是向他的叔叔良兼求娶他的女儿，也就是他的表妹，作为自己的妻子。

sentences.en: And Yoshikane says, no, I'm not interested in you.
sentences.zh: 良兼说，不，我对你不感兴趣。

sentences.en: You're just a samurai.
sentences.zh: 你只是个武士。

sentences.en: You know, you don't really rank as a member of my family anymore.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你真的不再算是我家族的一员了。

sentences.en: And Mascado is incredibly insulted by this and goes absolutely berserk.
sentences.zh: 将门对此感到无比羞辱，彻底暴走了。

sentences.en: So one minute he is quarreling with Yoshikane about his wedding plan, saying that he, you know, demanding to marry his cousin.
sentences.zh: 前一分钟他还在和良兼争论他的婚事，你知道，要求娶他的表妹，

sentences.en: And the next, he's been refused by Yoshikane, goes completely ballistic and starts torching entire villages,
sentences.zh: 后一分钟，在被良兼拒绝后，他彻底失控，开始焚烧整个村庄，

sentences.en: simply because these villages are dependencies of one of Yoshikane's allies.
sentences.zh: 仅仅因为这些村庄是良兼盟友的属地。

sentences.en: And we have a near contemporaneous account.
sentences.zh: 我们有一份近乎同时代的记载。

sentences.en: So this isn't kind of written up decades later.
sentences.zh: 所以这不是几十年后才写出来的。

sentences.en: This is kind of from around the time.
sentences.zh: 这是来自那个时代左右的记录。

sentences.en: That day, the voice of the flames contended with the thunder as it echoed.
sentences.zh: 那一天，火焰的声音与回荡的雷声争鸣。

sentences.en: That hour, the color of the smoke battled with the clouds as it covered the sky.
sentences.zh: 那一刻，烟雾的颜色与云朵搏斗，遮蔽了天空。

sentences.en: People's homes were turned to ashes and scattered before the winds.
sentences.zh: 人们的家园化为灰烬，在风中飘散。

sentences.en: Provincial officials and peasants alike beheld it all in anguish.
sentences.zh: 地方官员和农民们都痛苦地目睹了这一切。

sentences.en: And so Yoshikane obviously is infuriated by this.
sentences.zh: 所以良兼显然对此感到愤怒。

sentences.en: I mean, insulted.
sentences.zh: 我是说，受到了侮辱。

sentences.en: You know, he has to have vengeance.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他必须复仇。

sentences.en: And so he raises an enormous army, which Mascado, at the head of only 100 horsemen, spectacularly routes.
sentences.zh: 于是他集结了一支庞大的军队，但将门仅率领100名骑兵就将其壮观地击溃了。

sentences.en: It's an incredible victory, tribute to Mascado's charisma and to his mastery of the arts of warfare.
sentences.zh: 这是一场不可思议的胜利，是对将门的个人魅力和他对战争艺术掌握的致敬。

sentences.en: And so now things really are kicking off.
sentences.zh: 所以现在事情真的闹大了。

sentences.en: Mascado has taken his cousin, married her.
sentences.zh: 将门带走了他的表妹，并娶了她。

sentences.en: Yoshikane kidnaps her back.
sentences.zh: 良兼又把她绑架了回去。

sentences.en: According to the kind of the romantic version of this story, Mascado then sneaks behind enemy lines to meet her and does so with the connivance of his wife's brothers.
sentences.zh: 根据这个故事的浪漫版本，将门随后潜入敌后去见她，并且是在他妻子的兄弟们的默许下完成的。

sentences.en: So he's also his cousins.
sentences.zh: 所以他们也是他的表兄弟。

sentences.en: So there's a sense there of a kind of, you know, a real kind of dynastic snarl romance and hatreds and rivalries and all of that.
sentences.zh: 所以这里有一种感觉，你知道，一种真正的王朝纠葛、浪漫、仇恨、竞争等等。

sentences.en: And this is intensified by the fact that Mascado's cousin, a very sinister man called Sadamori, has signed up to Mascado's side and then promptly stabbed him in the back,
sentences.zh: 而这一点因为将门的表兄弟，一个非常阴险的人叫贞盛，他加入了将门一方，然后迅速在背后捅了他一刀而加剧，

sentences.en: betrayed him, acted as the agent of Yoshikane.
sentences.zh: 背叛了他，充当了良兼的代理人。

sentences.en: And even worse, Sadamori then rushes off to Kyoto, basically to tell tales on Mascado.
sentences.zh: 更糟糕的是，贞盛随后冲向京都，基本上是去告将门的状。

sentences.en: And as a reward for this, Sadamori is given the northern command that had been held by Mascado's father and which Mascado himself obviously had been hoping to get.
sentences.zh: 作为奖励，贞盛获得了原本由将门父亲担任的北方指挥权，而将门本人显然一直希望得到这个职位。

sentences.en: So again, it's an incredible insult to Mascado and makes him even more determined to have his vengeance.
sentences.zh: 所以这再次是对将门的极大侮辱，使他更加坚定了复仇的决心。

sentences.en: And this is a very fateful step because essentially what had begun as a kind of family feud is now starting to embroil the whole of Japan.
sentences.zh: 这是一个非常致命的步骤，因为本质上，这场始于家族纷争的事情现在开始卷入整个日本。

sentences.en: Mascado goes even further, doesn't he?
sentences.zh: 将门走得更远了，不是吗？

sentences.en: Doubles down.
sentences.zh: 加倍下注。

sentences.en: Because this is the point at which he can basically keep gambling or stop.
sentences.zh: 因为这是他基本上可以继续赌下去或者收手的时刻。

sentences.en: And he decides to keep gambling and he makes an extraordinary decision that he is going to declare himself emperor.
sentences.zh: 他决定继续赌下去，并做出了一个非凡的决定，他要自立为天皇。

sentences.en: So this basically takes us to that point I made earlier about, you know, why isn't it like the late Roman Empire where provincial governors are declaring themselves emperor?
sentences.zh: 所以这基本上把我们带到了我之前提到的那一点，你知道，为什么它不像罗马帝国晚期那样，地方总督自立为皇帝？

sentences.en: Well, now it is because this is what he's done.
sentences.zh: 嗯，现在就是了，因为这就是他所做的。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't declare himself the emperor of Kyoto, so the southwestern half of Japan.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他并没有宣布自己是京都的天皇，也就是日本西南部的一半。

sentences.en: He's specifically of Kanto, which is this kind of this great plain.
sentences.zh: 他专门是关东的天皇，也就是这片大平原。

sentences.en: And Mascado is the first and he will not be the last to recognize that Kanto is actually a much larger lowland region than Kansai, which is the plain on which Kyoto stands.
sentences.zh: 将门是第一个，也不会是最后一个认识到关东实际上比关西（京都所在的平原）大得多的低地地区的人。

sentences.en: And just to emphasize, Japan is three quarters mountain.
sentences.zh: 而且要强调的是，日本四分之三是山地。

sentences.en: So wherever, you know, the plains are absolutely crucial.
sentences.zh: 所以无论在哪里，你知道，平原绝对是至关重要的。

sentences.en: If you control a large, fertile plain, then you, you know, you're really motoring.
sentences.zh: 如果你控制了一片广阔肥沃的平原，那么，你知道，你就真的在飞速发展了。

sentences.en: And because Kanto is larger than Kansai, the plain on which Kyoto stands, then it means that potentially Kanto is a much richer and more powerful region.
sentences.zh: 而且因为关东比京都所在的关西平原更大，这意味着关东可能是一个更富裕、更强大的地区。

sentences.en: And even though Kyoto will remain the official capital of Japan for another a thousand years, in the long run, it is Mascado who will enjoy the last laugh.
sentences.zh: 尽管京都将在未来一千年里继续作为日本的官方首都，但从长远来看，笑到最后的是将门。

sentences.en: Because today, you know, it's not Kansai, but Kanto, which boasts Japan's and indeed perhaps the world's larger city.
sentences.zh: 因为今天，你知道，不是关西，而是关东，拥有日本乃至可能是世界上更大的城市。

sentences.en: And that is the city that comes to be known as Tokyo, the eastern capital.
sentences.zh: 那就是后来被称为东京的城市，东方之都。

sentences.en: So Mascado, by declaring himself the emperor of Kanto, you know, he is kind of looking to the future, but it is a very distant future.
sentences.zh: 所以将门通过自立为关东天皇，你知道，他是在展望未来，但这是一个非常遥远的未来。

sentences.en: Yeah, not his own future, unfortunately, for him.
sentences.zh: 是的，不幸的是，对他来说不是他自己的未来。

sentences.en: No, because by doing this, by declaring himself emperor of Kanto, effectively, he signed his own death warrant because the imperial authorities are not going to recognize his rule.
sentences.zh: 不，因为通过这样做，通过自立为关东天皇，他实际上签署了自己的死刑判决书，因为朝廷是不会承认他的统治的。

sentences.en: It's, you know, it's just unthinkable.
sentences.zh: 这，你知道，简直是不可思议的。

sentences.en: And so what they do is, you know, the classic course, they employ rival lords to bring Mascado down.
sentences.zh: 所以他们所做的是，你知道，经典的手段，他们雇佣敌对的领主来打倒将门。

sentences.en: And these rival lords, who include Sadamori, his cousin, are sponsored to turn on Mascado.
sentences.zh: 而这些敌对的领主，包括他的表兄弟贞盛，被资助去对付将门。

sentences.en: And they're given funds that enable them to fight through the winter.
sentences.zh: 他们得到了资金，使他们能够熬过冬天作战。

sentences.en: And this is something that Mascado doesn't have.
sentences.zh: 这是将门所没有的。

sentences.en: And so he is unable to sustain his own forces through the offseason.
sentences.zh: 所以他无法在淡季维持自己的军队。

sentences.en: And he's cornered.
sentences.zh: 他被逼到了绝境。

sentences.en: He's shot through the forehead, which is the one bit that his mother, the giant snake, hadn't been able to lick.
sentences.zh: 他的前额中箭，那是他母亲，那条巨蛇，没能舔到的地方。

sentences.en: So it splits his skull.
sentences.zh: 所以他的头骨裂开了。

sentences.en: And then he is decapitated.
sentences.zh: 然后他被斩首了。

sentences.en: And his head, of course, is then brought to Kyoto's, put on the marketplace.
sentences.zh: 当然，他的头颅随后被带到京都，放在市场上示众。

sentences.en: And it probably doesn't go flying off.
sentences.zh: 它可能并没有飞走。

sentences.en: And his fate does serve the lords of Japan and the samurai class more generally as a salutary warning.
sentences.zh: 他的命运确实给日本的领主和更广泛的武士阶层起到了警示作用。

sentences.en: And so his career, to that extent, you know, it's the exception that proves the rule.
sentences.zh: 所以他的职业生涯，在某种程度上，你知道，是证明规则的例外。

sentences.en: And, you know, several decades after the death of Mascado, the year 1000, this is the period when Lady Murasaki is writing the tale of Genji.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，在将门死后几十年，即1000年，这是紫式部撰写《源氏物语》的时期。

sentences.en: So it's 1,100 pages long.
sentences.zh: 所以它有1100页长。

sentences.en: And warfare in it is barely mentioned.
sentences.zh: 书中几乎没有提到战争。

sentences.en: And it never intrudes directly.
sentences.zh: 而且它从未直接介入。

sentences.en: It's the same with the Pillow book, isn't it, that we also did.
sentences.zh: 我们之前做的《枕草子》也是一样，不是吗？

sentences.en: Shea Shonigan's book.
sentences.zh: 清少纳言的书。

sentences.en: I mean, there's basically no fighting, no hint of battles, nothing, no sense of sort of disorder out there.
sentences.zh: 我是说，基本上没有战斗，没有战争的暗示，什么都没有，没有那种外界混乱的感觉。

sentences.en: And, you know, everything is incredibly ordered and perfect and elegant and all of this kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，一切都极其有序、完美、优雅，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And when we did that series on those two writers, we talked about how extraordinary this is in the context of what's going on in Western Europe in the same period.
sentences.zh: 当我们做关于那两位作家的系列节目时，我们谈到了在同一时期西欧发生的事情的背景下，这是多么非凡。

sentences.en: You know, it's Vikings.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是维京人。

sentences.en: It's Ethered the Unready.
sentences.zh: 那是埃塞尔雷德二世。

sentences.en: It's massacres.
sentences.zh: 那是大屠杀。

sentences.en: It's people, bishops being hit over the head with hammers.
sentences.zh: 那是人们，主教被锤子敲打头部。

sentences.en: It's just completely different.
sentences.zh: 这完全不同。

sentences.en: Whereas in the tale of Genji, it's not just that people aren't talking about war.
sentences.zh: 而在《源氏物语》中，不仅仅是人们不谈论战争。

sentences.en: They're not even talking about warriors.
sentences.zh: 他们甚至不谈论武士。

sentences.en: There are no warriors.
sentences.zh: 根本没有武士。

sentences.en: They just don't feature.
sentences.zh: 他们根本没有出现。

sentences.en: For people living in the court, this is, you know, a kind of paradisal age of peace and tranquility.
sentences.zh: 对于生活在朝廷的人来说，这是一个，你知道，一个和平与安宁的乐园时代。

sentences.en: And they are so secluded from the violence and the vulgarity of the provinces that they can enjoy the fruits of this brilliant civilization without having to worry about war.
sentences.zh: 他们与省份的暴力和粗俗隔绝，以至于他们可以享受这种辉煌文明的果实，而不必担心战争。

sentences.en: It's a world of beauty, of poetry, of love, of exquisite calligraphy, of beautiful perfumes.
sentences.zh: 这是一个充满美、诗歌、爱情、精致书法、美丽香气的世界。

sentences.en: You know, if you're into that kind of thing, it's tremendous.
sentences.zh: 你知道，如果你喜欢那种东西，那真是太棒了。

sentences.en: However, you know, history does not come to an end.
sentences.zh: 然而，你知道，历史并没有终结。

sentences.en: We see that for ourselves.
sentences.zh: 我们自己也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: And so it is for the courtiers in Heian Kyo in Kyoto.
sentences.zh: 平安京京都的朝臣们也是如此。

sentences.en: Because beyond the mountains, which ring the capital, the samurai are still very much there.
sentences.zh: 因为在环绕首都的群山之外，武士们依然存在。

sentences.en: And they are still learning the way of the bow and the horse.
sentences.zh: 他们仍在学习弓马之道。

sentences.en: And they're still being hired by governors of distant provinces as private mercenaries and being enrolled as their own retainers, as samurai.
sentences.zh: 他们仍然被遥远省份的总督雇佣为私人雇佣兵，并被招募为他们自己的家臣，即武士。

sentences.en: And still very much on the scene, and in fact, more powerful, more ambitious, more restless than ever, are these two great dynasties derived from the imperial house,
sentences.zh: 而且依然活跃在舞台上，事实上，比以往任何时候都更强大、更有野心、更不安分的是这两个源自皇室的伟大王朝，

sentences.en: the Taira and the Minamoto.
sentences.zh: 平氏和源氏。

sentences.en: And Dominic, it may not have been evident to the silken aristocrats cloistered in Kyoto, but the storm clouds of war were building.
sentences.zh: 多米尼克，对于那些深居京都的丝绸贵族来说，这可能并不明显，但战争的乌云正在聚集。

sentences.en: And the war that will come, this is a war that is going to end forever the dominance of the imperial court and establish in its place a dramatically new order.
sentences.zh: 而即将到来的战争，将永远终结朝廷的统治，并取而代之建立一个截然不同的新秩序。

sentences.en: Because the age of the courtier is coming to an end.
sentences.zh: 因为朝臣的时代即将结束。

sentences.en: The age of the samurai is dawning.
sentences.zh: 武士的时代正在黎明。

sentences.en: What a cliffhanger.
sentences.zh: 真是个悬念。

sentences.en: So we'll be returning to this brewing rivalry between the Taira and the Minamoto in the next episode, in which the age of the samurai dawns in earneSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我们将在下一集中回到平氏和源氏之间酝酿的竞争，在那一集中，武士时代将真正开启。

sentences.en: Now, if you want to hear that next episode literally right now, you can, if you're a member of the Rest is History Club, because you've got it already.
sentences.zh: 现在，如果你想现在就听到下一集，如果你是“历史的其余部分”俱乐部的成员，你可以听到，因为你已经拥有它了。

sentences.en: In fact, you don't just have to listen to that episode.
sentences.zh: 事实上，你不必只听那一集。

sentences.en: The next two episodes in this series are available to members of the Rest is History Club as well.
sentences.zh: 这个系列的接下来两集也提供给“历史的其余部分”俱乐部的成员。

sentences.en: Well, if you want to join that particular samurai warband and hear those episodes, then head to therestishistory.com and you get all kinds of unbelievable benefits as well,
sentences.zh: 好吧，如果你想加入那个特定的武士战团并收听这些剧集，那么前往therestishistory.com，你也会得到各种不可思议的好处，

sentences.en: including our exciting Super Soraway Newsletter, which has all kinds of extra content about the samurai and their age.
sentences.zh: 包括我们令人兴奋的“超级索拉威”通讯，其中有关于武士及其时代的所有额外内容。

sentences.en: So, on that bombshell, Tom, arigatou gozaimasu and sayonara, everybody.
sentences.zh: 那么，带着这个重磅消息，汤姆，谢谢大家，再见。

sentences.en: Matane.
sentences.zh: 回头见。
